messages.subject: unmarked occupancy for camera trap
parts:
Hi All, 

I am a total newbie in using the occupancy model so please forgive me I asked too many rookie questions. The aim of my study is to determine population estimate (size or density) of a single species of using data from camera traps. I am most interested to know the overall abundance but having site estimate will be a bonus for me but not necessary.There are 100 camera traps in total and they are randomly placed on a grid system within a single year. 

An example of the data input I currently have is :

                SIte           Grid                Count            Camerawork days
                  A                815                  3                         15
                  A                815                   0                         30
                  A                816                  2                         15
                  A                817                  0                         30
                  B                822                   1                        31             
                  B                823                  0                         30
                  C                825                   1                        31

The questions I have are:
(i) How should I input the data? at the moment I am putting the standardised count (= number of count/camera trap working daysX100) due to differences in the number of camera trap working days  
Am I correct in putting this? or should I input the actual count without standardising it and then use the camera trap working days as the covariate instead?

(ii) There are quite a few models and I am not very sure which model I should apply. I read a few other entries in the group and it seems that using the occuRN and pcount are also suitable for camera trap data. What the major differences between them?

Any comment will be appreciated!
Much thanks! 

Tam

messages.author: 474ec912731e50cf
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] unmarked occupancy for camera trap
parts:
Hi Tam

I work with camera traps in estimating abundance and density of two mammal species and I work with detection histories generated with package camtrapR, and this is the route to enter the data in occupancy models, these links could be usefull to you:

http://www.revmexmastozoologia.unam.mx/ojs/index.php/rmm/article/view/245
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/DataExtraction.html

For occuRN the data you have to use are detection histories of your species, due that this models work with detection/ not detection data, for each site and survey period. In case of N-mixture models the data to use are counts, but is important that you inspect if your records meet the assumptions of this models.

You can take a look of this book to undesrstand general concepts of models:
https://www.elsevier.com/books/applied-hierarchical-modeling-in-ecology-analysis-of-distribution-abundance-and-species-richness-in-r-and-bugs/kery/978-0-12-801378-6

Best regards,

Karen
